newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC in j/v talks to buy CVRD - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC in j/v talks to buy CVRD - paper.

text.p: Australian-based resources group WMC Ltd was negotiating to join a possible US$5 billion joint venture to buy a stake in Brazil's state-owned mining firm CVRD, The Australian newspaper reported on Friday.
"WMC has a team negotiating in Brazil which could result in the Australian mining house making an investment of more than US$1 billion," the newspaper said. It did not cite any sources.

"The team is involved win talks with several big miners, including South African-based Minorco and Gencor Ltd, about joining a consortium which would buy a 45 percent interest in Companhia Vale de Rio Doce (CRVD)," it said.

Last week the Brazilian government delayed the sale of the voting stake to April this year from the first quarter to allow independent analysts to evaluate new gold and copper finds before the government sets CVRD's base price.

The latest hiccup in the sale of the world's largest iron ore exporter came after a deluge of reports about "historic" finds in Carajas in Para state, near the existing Igarape Bahia gold mine and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.
Politicians opposed to the CVRD sell-off and newspapers also said Carajas could significantly alter the value of the company, an assertion some government officials conceded was possible.
The government last week hastened to reassure markets politics did not play a role in the decision to delay CVRD's privatization.
The asset sale is expected to begin with a block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares, followed by an internal offer to employees and then a public offering.
